questions.question: What is the primary purpose of DevSecOps?
questions.option_a: A. To replace software testing with automated security tools
questions.option_b: B. To integrate security into every stage of the Software Development Lifecycle
questions.option_c: C. To perform security assessments only before deployment
questions.option_d: D. To transfer all security responsibilities to the security team
questions.explanation: DevSecOps integrates security throughout the SDLC rather than treating it as a separate activity performed at the end. Security becomes a shared responsibility.

questions.question: What does the principle of shifting security left mean?
questions.option_a: A. Moving security activities to the maintenance phase
questions.option_b: B. Performing security assessments only after deployment
questions.option_c: C. Introducing security activities earlier in the development lifecycle
questions.option_d: D. Reducing the number of security tests during development
questions.explanation: Shifting security left means addressing security concerns as early as possible, particularly during requirements, design and implementation.

questions.question: Which statement best describes security responsibility in a DevSecOps environment?
questions.option_a: A. Security is a shared responsibility across development and operations teams
questions.option_b: B. Only penetration testers are responsible for security
questions.option_c: C. Developers are responsible only for functionality
questions.option_d: D. Security responsibility begins after software deployment
questions.explanation: DevSecOps establishes shared security responsibility across the teams involved in developing, deploying and maintaining software.

questions.question: A company discovers that security vulnerabilities are repeatedly identified immediately before production deployment. Which DevSecOps improvement would most directly address this problem?
questions.option_a: A. Increase the number of production servers
questions.option_b: B. Remove security testing from the development process
questions.option_c: C. Assign all security responsibilities to the operations team
questions.option_d: D. Integrate automated security checks and secure coding practices throughout development
questions.explanation: Integrating security throughout development identifies vulnerabilities earlier, reducing the likelihood of discovering major issues immediately before deployment.

questions.question: Which sequence correctly represents the Secure Software Development Lifecycle presented in the lecture?
questions.option_a: A. Design → Requirements → Testing → Development → Maintenance → Deployment
questions.option_b: B. Requirements → Design → Development → Testing → Deployment → Maintenance
questions.option_c: C. Requirements → Development → Deployment → Design → Testing → Maintenance
questions.option_d: D. Development → Requirements → Design → Maintenance → Testing → Deployment
questions.explanation: The lecture identifies six lifecycle phases in this order: Requirements, Design, Development, Testing, Deployment and Maintenance.

questions.question: During which SDLC phase should a team primarily identify how a proposed feature could be abused?
questions.option_a: A. Requirements
questions.option_b: B. Deployment
questions.option_c: C. Maintenance
questions.option_d: D. Operations
questions.explanation: During requirements, teams identify potential feature abuse and classify data. Abuse cases and data classification are important artifacts.

questions.question: Which security artifact is primarily produced during the design phase?
questions.option_a: A. Hardened deployment configuration
questions.option_b: B. SAST and DAST results
questions.option_c: C. Threat model
questions.option_d: D. Security incident alerts
questions.explanation: The design phase examines structural weaknesses and produces a threat model to identify potential threats and security risks.

questions.question: A development team wants to determine whether its running application can be broken by an attacker. Which SDLC phase and security activities are most appropriate?
questions.option_a: A. Requirements phase using data classification
questions.option_b: B. Design phase using architectural diagrams
questions.option_c: C. Deployment phase using secret management
questions.option_d: D. Testing phase using SAST and DAST
questions.explanation: Testing evaluates the security of the application. SAST and DAST results help identify vulnerabilities in source code and running applications.

questions.question: A company has successfully deployed an application. Which activity most directly supports the security objectives of the maintenance phase?
questions.option_a: A. Creating initial abuse cases
questions.option_b: B. Monitoring security logs, generating alerts and maintaining a patch process
questions.option_c: C. Designing the original database schema
questions.option_d: D. Writing the initial functional requirements
questions.explanation: Maintenance and operations involve detecting attacks, monitoring logs and alerts, and maintaining a process for applying security patches.

questions.question: Which statement most accurately defines secure coding?
questions.option_a: A. Writing code that executes as quickly as possible regardless of security
questions.option_b: B. Writing software that prevents users from accessing all sensitive functionality
questions.option_c: C. Writing software that protects against security vulnerabilities and attacks
questions.option_d: D. Writing code that requires manual security testing before every execution
questions.explanation: Secure coding is the practice of writing software that protects against vulnerabilities and attacks while improving reliability and resilience.

questions.question: Which vulnerability occurs when an attacker manipulates a database query through specially crafted user input?
questions.option_a: A. SQL Injection
questions.option_b: B. Cross-Site Request Forgery
questions.option_c: C. Buffer Overflow
questions.option_d: D. Broken Authentication
questions.explanation: SQL injection occurs when untrusted input is interpreted as part of an SQL command, potentially allowing an attacker to manipulate database operations.

questions.question: A malicious script is inserted into a webpage and executes in another user's browser. Which vulnerability does this describe?
questions.option_a: A. Command Injection
questions.option_b: B. Cross-Site Request Forgery
questions.option_c: C. Sensitive Data Exposure
questions.option_d: D. Cross-Site Scripting
questions.explanation: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) occurs when attacker-controlled content is executed as script in a victim's browser.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT identified as a common software vulnerability in the lecture?
questions.option_a: A. Buffer Overflow
questions.option_b: B. Cross-Site Request Forgery
questions.option_c: C. Database Normalization
questions.option_d: D. Command Injection
questions.explanation: Database normalization is a database design technique, not a security vulnerability. The lecture identifies SQL injection, XSS, CSRF, buffer overflow, command injection, broken authentication and sensitive data exposure.

questions.question: Which combination represents secure coding best practices?
questions.option_a: A. Trust user input, store passwords in plaintext and use administrator accounts
questions.option_b: B. Validate inputs, encode outputs, use parameterized queries and apply least privilege
questions.option_c: C. Disable error handling, hard-code credentials and avoid software updates
questions.option_d: D. Allow unrestricted database access and rely exclusively on frontend validation
questions.explanation: These practices directly reduce common application vulnerabilities, protect data and limit the impact of security compromises.

questions.question: A web application accepts data through forms, URL parameters, uploaded files and API requests. Which approach best represents secure input handling?
questions.option_a: A. Validate only data received through web forms
questions.option_b: B. Assume API requests are trustworthy because they originate from authenticated clients
questions.option_c: C. Validate inputs only when database errors occur
questions.option_d: D. Validate all externally originating data before using it
questions.explanation: All externally originating data must be checked against expected requirements, regardless of whether it comes from forms, URLs, files or API requests.

questions.question: Which validation rule determines whether a quantity falls between 1 and 100?
questions.option_a: A. Format validation
questions.option_b: B. Length validation
questions.option_c: C. Range validation
questions.option_d: D. Allowed-character validation
questions.explanation: Range validation checks whether a value falls within an acceptable minimum and maximum. The lecture uses a quantity range of 1 to 100.

questions.question: A registration system accepts usernames containing only letters, numbers and underscores, with a length between 3 and 20 characters. Which validation approach is most appropriate?
questions.option_a: A. Allowlist validation using an explicit pattern and length restriction
questions.option_b: B. Blocklist validation that removes apostrophes
questions.option_c: C. Output encoding without input validation
questions.option_d: D. Accept all input and depend on database constraints
questions.explanation: An allowlist explicitly defines permitted characters and length. A pattern such as [A-Za-z0-9_]{3,20} rejects inputs outside the expected format.

questions.question: What is the main weakness of blocklist-based input validation?
questions.option_a: A. It rejects every valid input by default
questions.option_b: B. It cannot validate the length of an input
questions.option_c: C. It requires all inputs to be converted into SQL statements
questions.option_d: D. It may fail against new attack variations that are not included in the blocklist
questions.explanation: Blocklists enumerate known malicious inputs. Attackers can bypass them using variations, encoding tricks or previously unknown patterns.

questions.question: Why is allowlist validation generally considered safer than blocklist validation?
questions.option_a: A. It automatically encrypts all incoming data
questions.option_b: B. It defines acceptable input and rejects everything outside that definition
questions.option_c: C. It automatically removes every malicious character
questions.option_d: D. It eliminates the need for output encoding
questions.explanation: Allowlist validation fails closed by accepting only explicitly permitted input. Unknown or unexpected values are rejected by default.

questions.question: Consider the following validation implementation: username = input.replace("'", "").replace("--", ""). What is its primary security weakness?
questions.option_a: A. It performs excessive output encoding
questions.option_b: B. It prevents all usernames from being stored
questions.option_c: C. It attempts to remove known dangerous patterns instead of defining valid input
questions.option_d: D. It automatically grants excessive database privileges
questions.explanation: Removing known dangerous characters is a blocklist-style approach. Attackers may bypass it using alternative representations or unanticipated input variations.

questions.question: A registration system receives the username <script>alert("XSS")</script>. The application expects usernames containing only letters, numbers and underscores. What should happen?
questions.option_a: A. Reject the input because it violates the allowed-character rule
questions.option_b: B. Accept the input and execute the script to check its behavior
questions.option_c: C. Remove the script tag and automatically accept the remaining value
questions.option_d: D. Store the input as an administrator username
questions.explanation: The input violates the defined username allowlist. The lecture explicitly recommends rejecting invalid input rather than correcting it and using it.

questions.question: A registration system receives the following values: Name = John123, Email = john.gmail.com, Age = -15, Quantity = 5000 and Username = <script>alert("XSS")</script>. Which assessment is most accurate?
questions.option_a: A. Every value should be accepted because the fields contain non-empty data
questions.option_b: B. Only the email should be rejected because the other fields are syntactically valid
questions.option_c: C. Age and quantity should be accepted because they are numerical values
questions.option_d: D. The email, age, quantity and username violate expected validation rules, while the name requires an explicitly defined name policy
questions.explanation: The email has an invalid format, age violates a reasonable positive-age range, quantity exceeds the specified acceptable range, and the username violates the allowed-character policy. John123 cannot be judged without a defined name policy.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of canonicalization before input validation?
questions.option_a: A. To encrypt input before database insertion
questions.option_b: B. To convert input into a single standard representation before applying security checks
questions.option_c: C. To replace parameterized queries with string concatenation
questions.option_d: D. To convert all input into executable code
questions.explanation: Canonicalization converts input into a standard representation so validation cannot be bypassed through alternative encodings or representations.

questions.question: An application checks a URL parameter for prohibited characters before decoding percent-encoded content. What security problem can occur?
questions.option_a: A. The database automatically rejects all requests
questions.option_b: B. The application becomes unable to generate security logs
questions.option_c: C. Encoded characters may bypass validation and become dangerous after decoding
questions.option_d: D. Password hashing algorithms become ineffective
questions.explanation: Validation before canonicalization can miss encoded representations. The lecture specifies the order: decode and normalize first, then validate, then use.

questions.question: Which sequence correctly represents secure input processing according to the lecture?
questions.option_a: A. Decode and normalize → Validate → Use
questions.option_b: B. Validate → Use → Decode
questions.option_c: C. Encode → Execute → Validate
questions.option_d: D. Use → Normalize → Validate
questions.explanation: Input must first be converted into a canonical representation, then validated against expectations, and finally used.

questions.question: Why should developers prefer established framework security mechanisms over manually implemented security controls?
questions.option_a: A. Frameworks eliminate the need for security testing
questions.option_b: B. Frameworks guarantee that every application is vulnerability-free
questions.option_c: C. Frameworks automatically remove the need for authentication
questions.option_d: D. Established frameworks provide maintained and reviewed implementations of security functionality
questions.explanation: Established frameworks provide validated and maintained implementations for validation, encoding, authentication and session handling. Handwritten security code may receive less review and fewer updates.

questions.question: A developer uses a template engine that automatically escapes HTML output but explicitly disables escaping for one user-controlled field. What is the most important security concern?
questions.option_a: A. The database will automatically reject the field
questions.option_b: B. The application may expose users to cross-site scripting through unencoded output
questions.option_c: C. The application will automatically enforce least privilege
questions.option_d: D. The application will prevent all session-related attacks
questions.explanation: Disabling automatic output escaping can allow attacker-controlled content to be interpreted as executable browser code. Framework security controls should not be bypassed without a valid reason and appropriate safeguards.

questions.question: What is the defining characteristic of a parameterized SQL query?
questions.option_a: A. User input is appended directly to the SQL command
questions.option_b: B. User input is encrypted before being concatenated into SQL
questions.option_c: C. SQL command structure and user-supplied values are transmitted separately
questions.option_d: D. SQL commands are executed using unrestricted database privileges
questions.explanation: Parameterized queries separate the SQL command structure from user-supplied values, ensuring that input is treated as data rather than SQL instructions.

questions.question: Consider the following query: SELECT * FROM users WHERE username = '" + username + "'; What is its main security weakness?
questions.option_a: A. It concatenates untrusted input into the SQL command
questions.option_b: B. It automatically encrypts the username
questions.option_c: C. It uses a prepared statement
questions.option_d: D. It prevents attackers from modifying query logic
questions.explanation: Direct concatenation allows attacker-controlled input to change the SQL query structure, creating an SQL injection vulnerability.

questions.question: Which implementation correctly uses parameterized SQL in Python according to the lecture?
questions.option_a: A. cursor.execute("SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = '" + name + "'")
questions.option_b: B. cursor.execute("SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = % name")
questions.option_c: C. cursor.execute("SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = '" + escape(name) + "'")
questions.option_d: D. cursor.execute("SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = ?", (name,))
questions.explanation: The placeholder and separately supplied parameter ensure that the database treats the username as data rather than part of the SQL command.

questions.question: An application constructs a login query by concatenating user input. An attacker supplies admin'-- as the username. What is the intended effect of this input in a vulnerable SQL query?
questions.option_a: A. It automatically creates a new administrator account
questions.option_b: B. It attempts to terminate the username condition and comment out the remaining SQL query
questions.option_c: C. It encrypts the password comparison
questions.option_d: D. It forces the database to execute a prepared statement
questions.explanation: In the vulnerable query pattern shown in the lecture, the apostrophe can terminate the string and the SQL comment marker can cause the remaining query, including a password check, to be ignored.

questions.question: An attacker submits ' OR '1'='1 as a username to an application using SQL string concatenation. Why can this attack return multiple database records?
questions.option_a: A. It automatically grants SELECT permission to the attacker
questions.option_b: B. It disables the database authentication mechanism
questions.option_c: C. It can modify the WHERE condition into a logically true expression
questions.option_d: D. It converts the database into an unrestricted file server
questions.explanation: The injected expression can cause the WHERE condition to evaluate as true for multiple rows, potentially returning all matching records.

questions.question: A developer claims that removing apostrophes and SQL comment markers is sufficient to protect an application against SQL injection. Which response is most accurate?
questions.option_a: A. The approach is sufficient if the database contains fewer than 1,000 records
questions.option_b: B. The approach is sufficient if input comes from authenticated users
questions.option_c: C. The approach is sufficient when the application uses HTTPS
questions.option_d: D. The approach is unreliable because input filtering cannot guarantee separation of SQL commands and data; parameterized queries should be used
questions.explanation: The definitive SQL injection defense presented in the lecture is parameterization. Filtering known dangerous characters does not reliably prevent query manipulation.

questions.question: What is the fundamental difference between authentication and authorization?
questions.option_a: A. Authentication determines identity, while authorization determines permitted access
questions.option_b: B. Authentication determines database structure, while authorization encrypts passwords
questions.option_c: C. Authentication controls logging, while authorization controls software updates
questions.option_d: D. Authentication validates input, while authorization performs output encoding
questions.explanation: Authentication answers who a user is. Authorization determines what that authenticated user is allowed to access or perform.

questions.question: Which combination represents authentication best practices identified in the lecture?
questions.option_a: A. Hard-coded passwords, unlimited login attempts and shared sessions
questions.option_b: B. Administrator access for all users and plaintext password storage
questions.option_c: C. MFA, strong password policies, secure password hashing, failed-login limits and secure session management
questions.option_d: D. Output encoding, SQL parameterization and database normalization
questions.explanation: The lecture identifies MFA, strong password policies, secure password hashing, limiting failed login attempts and secure session management as authentication best practices.

questions.question: A university portal has Student, Lecturer, Department Head and System Administrator roles. Which access-control approach is most appropriate for managing their different permissions?
questions.option_a: A. Giving every user identical permissions
questions.option_b: B. Role-Based Access Control
questions.option_c: C. Allowing users to define their own permissions
questions.option_d: D. Disabling authorization after successful login
questions.explanation: RBAC assigns permissions according to predefined roles. It is suitable for systems with distinct user categories and different access requirements.

questions.question: A student successfully logs into a university portal but attempts to access a lecturer-only endpoint. Which security control should prevent this operation?
questions.option_a: A. Password hashing
questions.option_b: B. Input length validation
questions.option_c: C. Multi-factor authentication alone
questions.option_d: D. Authorization and permission verification for the requested resource
questions.explanation: Successful authentication does not grant permission to access every resource. The application must verify authorization for each protected request.

questions.question: A university system implements RBAC but checks permissions only when users log in. A student logs in and later changes a URL to access another student's private results. What is the primary weakness?
questions.option_a: A. The application fails to verify permissions for every request and resource
questions.option_b: B. The application uses an unnecessarily strong password policy
questions.option_c: C. The application performs excessive output encoding
questions.option_d: D. The application stores security events in a log file
questions.explanation: Authorization must be verified for every request. A successful login or initial role check must not be treated as permanent permission to access arbitrary resources.

questions.question: Which statement best describes the principle of least privilege in authorization?
questions.option_a: A. Every authenticated user receives administrative access
questions.option_b: B. Users should receive additional permissions whenever they request them
questions.option_c: C. Users and components should receive only the permissions necessary to perform their functions
questions.option_d: D. Permissions should be checked only during account creation
questions.explanation: Least privilege limits access to the minimum permissions required for a particular function, reducing opportunities for unauthorized actions.

questions.question: An online banking application wants to investigate suspicious activities. Which collection of events is most valuable for security logging?
questions.option_a: A. Only successful customer registrations
questions.option_b: B. Only application startup and shutdown times
questions.option_c: C. Every database record, including passwords and authentication secrets
questions.option_d: D. Failed login attempts, authentication failures, access violations and relevant security events
questions.explanation: Security logs should capture meaningful events that support detection and accountability, including failed authentication attempts and unauthorized access.

questions.question: Which information should never be recorded in ordinary application security logs?
questions.option_a: A. Failed authentication timestamps
questions.option_b: B. Plaintext passwords, session tokens and full payment card security data
questions.option_c: C. Access violation events
questions.option_d: D. Security event identifiers
questions.explanation: Sensitive credentials and authentication secrets should not be exposed through logs. This is a general secure logging practice; the lecture identifies logging events but does not enumerate prohibited log contents.

questions.question: Why is secure logging important during incident investigations?
questions.option_a: A. It automatically prevents every security vulnerability
questions.option_b: B. It eliminates the need for authentication
questions.option_c: C. It provides evidence of security events that helps investigators understand and reconstruct suspicious activities
questions.option_d: D. It ensures that attackers cannot access the application
questions.explanation: Security logs provide evidence of events, supporting detection, accountability and investigation of security incidents.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT listed as an OWASP Secure Coding Practices focus area in the lecture?
questions.option_a: A. Password management
questions.option_b: B. Communication security
questions.option_c: C. File management
questions.option_d: D. Increasing processor clock speed
questions.explanation: OWASP focus areas in the lecture include password management, communication security, file management, input validation, output encoding, access control, cryptography and several other security practices. Processor clock speed is unrelated.

questions.question: Which mapping correctly associates a secure coding habit with the vulnerability or risk it addresses?
questions.option_a: A. Input validation — SQL injection, logic abuse and overflow; parameterization — SQL injection; output encoding — XSS; least privilege — escalation after compromise
questions.option_b: B. Input validation — password hashing; parameterization — CSRF; output encoding — buffer overflow; least privilege — XSS
questions.option_c: C. Input validation — session management; parameterization — broken authentication; output encoding — SQL injection; least privilege — CSRF
questions.option_d: D. Input validation — encryption; parameterization — memory management; output encoding — database normalization; least privilege — input formatting
questions.explanation: This mapping follows the lecture's summary table connecting the four secure coding habits to the vulnerabilities they prevent.

questions.question: A company wants to identify important assets in its Learning Management System. Which set contains five appropriate assets?
questions.option_a: A. Phishing, malware, SQL injection, XSS and CSRF
questions.option_b: B. Students, lecturers, attackers, administrators and competitors
questions.option_c: C. Student records, examination results, authentication credentials, course materials and financial records
questions.option_d: D. Weak passwords, missing patches, excessive permissions, insecure APIs and outdated software
questions.explanation: Assets are valuable resources that require protection. The listed records, credentials and educational materials are examples of valuable LMS assets.

questions.question: Which option correctly distinguishes a threat from a vulnerability?
questions.option_a: A. A threat is always a software defect, while a vulnerability is always a person
questions.option_b: B. A threat is a potential source of harm, while a vulnerability is a weakness that can be exploited
questions.option_c: C. A threat is a valuable resource, while a vulnerability is a security control
questions.option_d: D. A threat and a vulnerability are identical concepts
questions.explanation: A threat represents a potential source of harm, whereas a vulnerability is a weakness that may allow that threat to affect a system.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a threat actor targeting a university LMS?
questions.option_a: A. An unpatched software library
questions.option_b: B. An exposed database password
questions.option_c: C. A missing input validation mechanism
questions.option_d: D. A malicious student attempting to obtain unauthorized examination results
questions.explanation: A threat actor is an individual or group capable of carrying out an attack. A malicious student attempting unauthorized access is an example.

questions.question: A university LMS stores examination results in a database. An attacker exploits a SQL injection vulnerability to retrieve confidential records. Which classification is most accurate?
questions.option_a: A. Examination results are an asset, the attacker is a threat actor, SQL injection is a vulnerability, and unauthorized data disclosure is the resulting threat impact
questions.option_b: B. Examination results are a threat actor, SQL injection is an asset, and the attacker is a vulnerability
questions.option_c: C. The attacker is an asset, examination results are a vulnerability, and SQL injection is a mitigation
questions.option_d: D. SQL injection is a threat actor, the database is a vulnerability, and the attacker is an asset
questions.explanation: The database records are valuable assets, the malicious attacker is the threat actor, and the SQL injection weakness provides a path to unauthorized data disclosure.

questions.question: Which mitigation most directly addresses unauthorized access caused by weak application permissions?
questions.option_a: A. Increasing the number of application servers
questions.option_b: B. Disabling security logging
questions.option_c: C. Implementing least privilege and enforcing authorization checks
questions.option_d: D. Allowing users to access resources through direct URLs
questions.explanation: Least privilege and permission verification limit access to authorized users and reduce the potential impact of compromised accounts.

questions.question: A university performs a security assessment of its LMS. Which set correctly represents five different threat categories or sources that could affect the system?
questions.option_a: A. Weak passwords, outdated libraries, insecure APIs, missing patches and excessive privileges
questions.option_b: B. Phishing, unauthorized account access, malware, denial-of-service attacks and insider misuse
questions.option_c: C. Student records, lecturer records, examination results, course materials and credentials
questions.option_d: D. Input validation, output encoding, password hashing, logging and MFA
questions.explanation: The items in option B describe potential threats or attack activities. Option A describes vulnerabilities, option C describes assets and option D describes security controls.

questions.question: A web application validates an input using an allowlist but stores the value and later displays it in an HTML page. Which statement best describes the application's remaining security requirement?
questions.option_a: A. Input validation alone guarantees that the value cannot execute as a script in every output context
questions.option_b: B. Output encoding is unnecessary when the input has been stored in a database
questions.option_c: C. The application should disable all template escaping to preserve the original input
questions.option_d: D. The application should also apply appropriate output encoding when displaying the value
questions.explanation: Input validation and output encoding are complementary. Even validated input should be encoded appropriately for its destination context when displayed.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of output encoding in preventing XSS?
questions.option_a: A. To convert special characters into harmless representations so the browser displays them rather than executing them
questions.option_b: B. To remove all user-generated content from the database
questions.option_c: C. To encrypt the entire HTML document before it reaches the browser
questions.option_d: D. To prevent users from submitting HTTP requests
questions.explanation: Output encoding replaces characters with safe representations appropriate to the destination context, preventing attacker-controlled text from being interpreted as executable code.

questions.question: An application stores the string <script>alert(1)</script> in a database. Later, it displays the value without encoding it. What is the most likely result?
questions.option_a: A. The database automatically removes the script element
questions.option_b: B. The browser displays the string as harmless text in every case
questions.option_c: C. The browser may interpret the value as HTML and execute the script
questions.option_d: D. The application automatically converts the script into a parameterized SQL query
questions.explanation: Unencoded attacker-controlled HTML can be parsed by the browser, potentially resulting in script execution and XSS.

questions.question: An application correctly encodes user input in HTML body content but inserts the same input into a JavaScript string without JavaScript-context encoding. What is the primary problem?
questions.option_a: A. HTML body encoding automatically protects every other output context
questions.option_b: B. Output encoding must match the destination context; HTML encoding alone is insufficient for JavaScript contexts
questions.option_c: C. The application needs to replace all parameterized queries with concatenation
questions.option_d: D. The application must disable authentication before displaying JavaScript
questions.explanation: The lecture identifies HTML body, HTML attribute, JavaScript and URL as different output contexts. Encoding must be appropriate to the context in which the data is used.

questions.question: A user submits a malicious script to a university discussion forum. The application stores the input and displays it to other students. Which security combination is most appropriate?
questions.option_a: A. Database administrator privileges and unrestricted HTML rendering
questions.option_b: B. Blocklist filtering alone and disabled browser security
questions.option_c: C. Authentication alone and unrestricted output rendering
questions.option_d: D. Validate incoming data and encode the stored value appropriately when displayed
questions.explanation: Input validation rejects data outside the application's requirements, while context-appropriate output encoding prevents accepted or stored data from being interpreted as executable script.

questions.question: What does least privilege mean when applied to an application's database account?
questions.option_a: A. The application should connect using the database administrator account
questions.option_b: B. The application should receive all permissions so future development becomes easier
questions.option_c: C. The application should receive only the database permissions required for its actual operations
questions.option_d: D. The application should use a different database account for every individual query
questions.explanation: A restricted database account should have only the permissions needed to perform its functions, reducing the impact of a compromise.

questions.question: An application only reads product information and creates customer orders. Which database permission configuration most closely follows least privilege?
questions.option_a: A. GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON shop.* TO 'app'@'%'
questions.option_b: B. Grant SELECT on products and the necessary SELECT and INSERT permissions on orders, without administrative or unrelated privileges
questions.option_c: C. Grant DROP, DELETE and ALTER on every database table
questions.option_d: D. Grant unrestricted access to administrator accounts and customer credentials
questions.explanation: Permissions should match actual application functionality. The account needs only the relevant read and write operations, not unrestricted database access.

questions.question: A compromised application account has SELECT, INSERT and UPDATE permissions on shop.orders and SELECT permissions on shop.products. It has no access to shop.admin_users and cannot DROP tables. What security benefit does this configuration provide?
questions.option_a: A. It guarantees that SQL injection is impossible
questions.option_b: B. It prevents every form of unauthorized access
questions.option_c: C. It eliminates the need for database backups
questions.option_d: D. It limits the attacker's capabilities and reduces the potential damage of a compromise
questions.explanation: Restricted database privileges limit the blast radius. Even if an attacker exploits the application, the compromised account cannot perform operations for which it lacks permission.

questions.question: An application uses parameterized queries correctly but runs its database connection with full administrative privileges. Which statement best evaluates this architecture?
questions.option_a: A. Parameterization and least privilege address different security risks; the application should still use restricted database permissions
questions.option_b: B. Parameterized queries automatically remove all database privileges
questions.option_c: C. Administrative privileges are required for every parameterized query
questions.option_d: D. Least privilege applies only to operating system users, not database accounts
questions.explanation: Parameterized queries prevent SQL injection through query structure and data separation. Least privilege limits the impact of a compromise. Both controls are necessary because they address different risks.

questions.question: Which tool combination is associated with checking parameterized query and output encoding practices in the lecture?
questions.option_a: A. Parameterized queries: ZAP only; output encoding: IAM audit only
questions.option_b: B. Parameterized queries: manual review only; output encoding: database backups
questions.option_c: C. Parameterized queries: Semgrep and SonarQube; output encoding: Semgrep and ZAP
questions.option_d: D. Parameterized queries: IAM audit; output encoding: password hashing
questions.explanation: The lecture maps parameterized query checks to Semgrep and SonarQube, while output encoding checks are associated with Semgrep and ZAP.

questions.question: A security team wants to assess whether an application follows all four secure coding habits. Which combination of review activities best matches the lecture?
questions.option_a: A. Check input validation, parameterized queries, output encoding and least-privilege permissions
questions.option_b: B. Check application colors, page loading speed, database size and user interface layout
questions.option_c: C. Check only password complexity and server uptime
questions.option_d: D. Check only whether the application uses HTTPS and a firewall
questions.explanation: The four foundational secure coding habits are validating all input, using parameterized queries, encoding output and applying least privilege.

questions.question: A company is developing an online healthcare management system. During requirements, the team identifies patient records as highly sensitive and documents possible abuse of appointment and medical-record features. Which statement best describes the security work being performed?
questions.option_a: A. Deployment hardening and secret management
questions.option_b: B. Maintenance monitoring and patch management
questions.option_c: C. Dynamic application security testing
questions.option_d: D. Requirements-phase abuse-case identification and data classification
questions.explanation: The requirements phase identifies how features could be abused and classifies sensitive data. These activities guide security decisions in later phases.

questions.question: A banking application records successful and failed login attempts, but it also writes users' plaintext passwords and session tokens into the same log files. Which assessment is most accurate?
questions.option_a: A. The logging implementation is fully secure because it records authentication events
questions.option_b: B. The logging implementation is unsafe because sensitive authentication information is exposed in logs
questions.option_c: C. Logging should be disabled because security events are not useful
questions.option_d: D. Session tokens should be logged in plaintext to improve accountability
questions.explanation: Security events should be logged for detection and accountability, but sensitive credentials and session secrets must not be exposed in logs.

questions.question: A university LMS has the following weaknesses: outdated software, weak passwords, unrestricted database privileges, missing input validation and inadequate access controls. Which approach represents the most comprehensive mitigation strategy?
questions.option_a: A. Increase server capacity and leave existing security controls unchanged
questions.option_b: B. Disable logging to reduce operational complexity
questions.option_c: C. Apply software updates, strengthen authentication, validate inputs, restrict database permissions and enforce authorization
questions.option_d: D. Allow unrestricted access to all university users after login
questions.explanation: The proposed mitigations directly address the identified vulnerabilities through secure coding, authentication, authorization, least privilege and software maintenance.

questions.question: A developer implements the following controls: (1) accepts only usernames matching an allowlist, (2) uses prepared statements, (3) HTML-encodes displayed user content, and (4) connects to the database using restricted permissions. Which option correctly identifies the main security purpose of each control?
questions.option_a: A. (1) XSS prevention only, (2) password protection, (3) SQL injection prevention, (4) session management
questions.option_b: B. (1) Authentication, (2) authorization, (3) database normalization, (4) input validation
questions.option_c: C. (1) Data encryption, (2) access logging, (3) password hashing, (4) CSRF prevention
questions.option_d: D. (1) Input validation, (2) SQL injection prevention, (3) XSS prevention, (4) limiting compromise impact through least privilege
questions.explanation: The four controls correspond directly to the four foundational secure coding habits and their associated security objectives.
